overview: Identify discontinued shingles/siding, leverage iTel and manufacturer documentation, cite matching laws and codes, and navigate special scenarios to secure full approvals.
learningObjectives: Identify English vs. Metric dimensions and why they cannot be mixed
Verify discontinuation using iTel and manufacturer resources
Apply matching law arguments (e.g., Maryland Bulletin 18-23)
Cite code compliance (e.g., VA R905.2.2 low slope; MD IRC R703.2 WRB)
Document failed repair attempts and escalations

sections.title: Discontinued Product Identification
sections.content: English vs. Metric exposure differences; older architectural lines; 3‑tab lines often discontinued (GAF Royal Sovereign, CertainTeed XT 25, Owens Corning Supreme). Visual cues and catalog checks.

sections.title: iTel & Manufacturer Verification
sections.content: Identify brand/model; research manufacturer; generate iTel report; attach to estimate; prove unavailability.

sections.title: Matching Law & Arguments
sections.content: ‘Like kind and quality’ policy language and Maryland Insurance Bulletin 18‑23. When no true match exists, argue for full replacement to avoid aesthetic mismatch.

sections.title: Code & Special Scenarios
sections.content: VA R905.2.2: Asphalt shingles not allowed below 2:12 slope. MD IRC R703.2: Water‑resistive barrier behind siding. Repair attempt failures: brittle test video and Repair Attempt Template.

activities.title: Identify Discontinued
activities.description: From photo description, identify likely discontinued.

data.scenario: Compose an email excerpt for a discontinued shingle: reference iTel, cite matching requirement, request full replacement.

quiz.question: Why can’t English and Metric dimension shingles be mixed?
quiz.explanation: Different exposures prevent proper sealing and create visible mismatch.
